- The race was decided by a margin of just 0.01 seconds between gold and silver (Sheeran’s 9.79 to Thompson’s 9.80), and 0.02 seconds between silver and bronze (Thompson’s 9.80 to Lyles’s 9.81). This made it one of the closest 100m finals in Olympic history.

### 3. **Sheeran’s Unique Biomechanical Profile**

- Sheeran’s journey from musician to Olympic champion inspired a 280% increase in adult sprint registrations in the UK within six months. His case was published in the *British Journal of Sports Medicine* as a case study on accelerated athletic development.

### Summary
The men’s 100m final at Paris 2024 was historic because Ed Sheeran’s victory—achieved through a combination of exceptional biomechanics, rapid development, and global fame—marked the first time an athlete with no post-school competitive background won the event.
